translations.text: In many parts and in many ways God spoke in the past to our fathers through the prophets; in these last days he has spoken to us through his own Son,
whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom also the ages were made.
He was the radiance of glory and the image of his power,
he bears all things by the word of his power. He made purification for our sins, and he sat down at the right hand of the riches [?] in the heights.
He became as much better than the angels as the name he inherited is more excellent than theirs.
For to which of the angels did he ever say: "You are my Son, and today I have begotten you"? And again he says: "I will be his Father, and he will be my Son."
And when he again brings the firstborn into the world, he says: "And let all the angels of God worship him."
Of the angels he says: "He makes his angels spirits and his servants a flame of fire."
But of the Son he says: "Your throne, O God, is for ever and ever; the scepter of right governance is the scepter of your kingdom.
You loved righteousness and hated lawlessness. Therefore God, your God, has anointed you with the oil of gladness above your companions."
And: "You, Lord, founded the earth in the beginning, and the heavens are the works of your hands;
they will perish, but you remain forever; and they will all grow old like garments,
and like a cloak you will change them, and they will be changed. But you are the same, and your years will not come to an end."
To which of the angels did he ever say: "Sit at my right hand until I put your enemies under your feet"?
Are they not all ministering spirits, sent out to serve those who are to inherit salvation?
Therefore we must pay greater attention to what we have heard, so that we do not grow weak.
For if the word spoken through angels proved firm, and every transgressor of the law and every disobedient person received the penalty of judgment in return,
how will we escape if we neglect so great a salvation? It began when the Lord spoke it, and those who heard him confirmed it to us,
while God testified along with them by signs and wonders and various powers, and by gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to his will.
For it was not to angels that he subjected the world to come, which we are speaking about.
Someone has testified somewhere, saying: "What is man, that you remember him? Or the son of man, that you look upon him?
You made him a little lower than your angels; you crowned him with glory and honor, and you set him over the work of your hands;
you subjected all things under his feet." In subjecting all things, he left nothing that was not subject to him. Yet we do not now see all things subjected to him.
But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, crowned with glory and honor because of the suffering of death, so that by the grace of God he might taste death for everyone.
For it was fitting for him, for whom all things exist and through whom all things exist, in bringing many sons to glory, to make the leader of their salvation perfect through sufferings.
For the one who sanctifies and those who are sanctified all come from one. For this reason he is not ashamed to call them brothers, and he says:
"I will tell your name to my brothers, and in the midst of the congregation I will sing praise to you."
And then he says, "I will trust in him"; and again he says, "Here I am, and the children whom God has given me."
For since the children shared in flesh and blood, he himself likewise took on the same things, so that through death he might destroy the one who had the power of death, that is, the devil,
and set free those who, through fear of death, were subject to oppression all their lives.
For he did not take his beginning from angels at all; he took his beginning from the race of Abraham.
Therefore he had to be made like his brothers in every way, so that he might become a merciful and faithful high priest before God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
Since he himself suffered and was tested, he is able to help those who are being tested too.
Therefore, holy brothers, sharers in the heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the apostle and high priest of your confession,
who is faithful to the one who made him, as Moses was in all his house.
For this one was considered worthy of more glory than Moses, just as the builder of a house has more honour than the house itself.
For every house is built by someone, but all things were built by God.
Moses too was faithful over all his house, as a servant, to bear witness to the things that would be spoken.
But Christ was faithful as a son over his house. For we are, as it were, houses, if we hold firmly to the end the boldness and the boast of hope.
Therefore, as the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear his voice,
do not harden your hearts as in that testing, as on the day of testing in the wilderness,
where your fathers tested me. They tested me and saw my works for forty years.
Therefore I grew weary of that generation and said, 'They always go astray in their hearts, and they have not known my ways.'
As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my rest."
Take care, brothers, that none of you has an evil heart of unbelief, so as to fall away from the living God.
Instead, encourage one another every day, while it is still called "today," so that none of you is hardened by the deceit of sin.
For we have become sharers in Christ, if we hold the beginning of our strength firmly to the end.
As for what was said: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts as in that provocation":
For some heard and rebelled, but not all of those who came out of Egypt under Moses.
With whom did he grow weary for forty years? Was it not with those who sinned, whose bones fell in the wilderness?
To whom did he swear that they would not enter his rest? Was it not to those who were disobedient?
And we see that they could not enter because of unbelief.
Let us therefore be afraid that, while the promise of entering his rest is still left open, any of you might think himself to have fallen short.
For the good news has been proclaimed to us, just as it was to them. But the word they heard did not benefit them, because faith was not mixed in with those who heard it.
But we who believe shall enter that rest, just as he said: "As I swore in my wrath, they shall not enter my rest"; and yet the works had been finished since the foundation of the world.
For somewhere he has spoken about the seventh day like this: "And God rested on the seventh day from all his works."
And after this he says again: "They shall not enter my rest."
So it remains for some to enter it, and those to whom the good news was proclaimed before did not enter because of unbelief.
So again he sets the same day, "Today", through David, saying after so long a time, as was said before: "Today, if you hear his voice, do not harden your hearts."
For if Joshua the son of Nun had brought them into that rest, he would not have spoken afterwards about another day.
Does a Sabbath rest then remain for the people of God?
For whoever has entered his rest has also rested from his own works, just as God rested from his.
Let us therefore hurry to enter that rest, so that no one may fall into the same example of unbelief.

For the word of God is living and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword. It reaches even to the dividing of soul and spirit, of joints and marrow, and it judges the hidden thoughts and intentions of the heart.
And no created thing is hidden before him. Everything is naked and laid bare (literally "with neck bent back") before the eyes of him about whom we are speaking.
We have a great high priest who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God; let us hold fast to that confession.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to have mercy on our weaknesses, but one who has been tested in every way just as we are, yet without sin.
Let us approach the throne of grace boldly, so that we may receive mercy and find grace at the time when we need help.
For every high priest is taken from among men and appointed on behalf of men in matters relating to God, to offer gifts and sacrifices for sins, for forgiveness,
and he is able to show fitting mercy to the ignorant and those who go astray, for he himself is also subject to weakness;
and because of this he is obliged to offer sacrifice for sins for himself as well as for the people.
And no one takes the honor for himself; only someone who is called by God takes it, as Aaron was.
So also Christ did not glorify himself to become high priest. It was the one who said to him: "You are my Son; today I have begotten you."
As he also says in another place: "You are a priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek."
In the days of his flesh he offered prayers and supplications with a loud voice and tears to the one who was able to save him from death, and he was heard because of his reverent fear.
And although he was the Son, he learned obedience from what he suffered;
And he was made perfect, and he became the cause of eternal life for all who obey him;
and he was named by God high priest according to the order of Melchizedek.
About him we have much to say, and it is hard to explain, because you have become weak in hearing.

For by this time you ought to have been teachers. Instead, you still need someone to teach you again some of the first principles of the words of God. You have become like people who need milk, not solid food.
For everyone who lives on milk is unskilled in the word of righteousness, because he is an infant.
But solid food belongs to the mature, who through that practice have their faculties trained to tell good from evil.
Therefore let us leave behind the first teaching about Christ and move on to what is more perfect. Let us not lay again a foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God,
of teaching about baptism and the laying on of hands, of the resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment.
And we will do this if God commands us.
For it is impossible for those who have once been baptized, who have tasted the heavenly gifts and have become partakers of the Holy Spirit,
and who have tasted the goodness of the word of God and the power of the ages to come,
and who then have sinned, to be renewed again to repentance, since they crucify themselves together with the Son of God and put him to open shame.
For the ground that drinks the rain that often falls on it, and brings forth green plants useful to those for whose sake it is cultivated, receives a blessing from God.
But the ground that brings forth thorns and thistles is worthless and close to being cursed, and in the end it will be burned.
But concerning you, beloved, we are confident of better things, things close to salvation, even though we speak this way.
For there is no falsehood with God that he would forget your works and the love you showed for his name, in that you served the saints and still serve them.
We want each one of you to show the same eagerness for the fulfilment of hope until the end,
so that you do not become sluggish, but imitate those who through faith and patience inherited the promises.
For when God made a promise to Abraham, since there was no one greater by whom he could swear, he swore by himself,
and said: "I will surely bless you and I will surely multiply you."
And so, after waiting patiently, he obtained the promise.
For people swear by someone greater than themselves, and an oath serves to confirm and settle all their disputes.
So God, wishing to show even more clearly to the heirs of the promise that his purpose cannot change, guaranteed it with an oath,
so that through these two unchangeable things, in which God cannot lie, we who have fled for refuge might have strong encouragement to hold fast to the hope set before us.
We hold this hope as an anchor of the soul, secure and firm, which enters the inner side of the veil,
where Jesus, the forerunner, entered for us, having become high priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of God Most High, who met Abraham when he was returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him,
to whom Abraham gave as a portion a tithe of everything, is first interpreted "king of righteousness," and then "king of Salem," which is king of peace,
without father, without mother, without recorded lineage; he has neither beginning of days nor end of life, he is made like the Son of God, and he remains a priest forever.
See, then, how great this man was, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tithe of the choicest spoils.

And those of the sons of Levi who receive the priesthood have a commandment to receive a tithe from the people according to the law, that is, from their own brothers, even though these too have come out of the loins of Abraham.
But to the one whose lineage is not recorded among them Abraham gave a tithe, and he blessed the one who had received the promise.
Beyond all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the better.
And here it is men who die who receive tithes, but there it is testified that he is alive.
And to put it briefly, through Abraham even Levi, who receives tithes, has himself been offered in tithe;
for he was still in his father's loins when Melchizedek met him.

If perfection had been through the Levites' priesthood (for on it the people have been given the law), what need was there for another priest to be raised up according to the order of Melchizedek, and not to be spoken of according to the order of Aaron?
For it appears that with the change of the priesthood there is also a change of the law,
since the one about whom this is said belonged to another tribe, from which no one had ever stood at the altar.
It is evident beforehand that our Lord has risen for us from the tribe of Judah, a tribe about which Moses said nothing concerning priesthood.
And it is clearer still if another high priest arises in the likeness of Melchizedek,
who is not so according to the law of a fleshly commandment, but according to the power of an unending life.
For it is testified of him: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek.
For that former commandment is set aside because of its weakness and uselessness,
for the law brought nothing to perfection; but there is the bringing in of a better hope, through which we draw near to God.
And inasmuch as it was not without an oath (for some became priests without an oath,
but this one with an oath, through him who said to him: The Lord has sworn and will not repent: You are a priest forever according to the order of Melchizedek),
by so much has Jesus also become the guarantor of a better covenant.
And those others are many who have been appointed priests, because they are prevented by death from remaining.
But this one has that priesthood unending, forever.
Therefore he is also fully able to give life to those who come to God through him, since he is ever living to intercede for them.
For such a high priest was fitting for us: holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sins and higher than the heavens,
who has no need day by day, like those high priests, to offer sacrifice first for his own sins and then for the people; but he himself did this once, when he offered himself.
For the law appointed as priests men who had weakness, but the word of the oath, which came after the law, appointed a Son, perfected forever.
Now the chief point of what has been said is this: we have such a high priest, who sat down at the right hand of the throne of glory in the heavens,
a minister of the holy things and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord erected and not man.
Every high priest is appointed to offer sacrifice and offering; for this reason it is fitting that he too have something that he may offer of his own.
If he were on earth, he would not be a priest, since there are those who offer, by whom sacrifices are offered according to the law,

who serve as a pattern and shadow of the heavenly things, just as Moses received a command concerning the work of the tabernacle, and he said to him: See that you make everything according to the pattern that was shown to you on the mountain.
But now he has attained a better ministry, inasmuch as he is mediator of a better covenant, which has been established by law upon that better promise.
If that first one had been blameless, no place would have been sought for the second,
for he reproaches them and says to them: Behold, the days are coming, says the Lord, and I will accomplish upon the house of Israel and upon the house of Judah a new covenant,

not like the covenant that I made with their fathers on the day when I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt; for they did not remain in my law, and I disregarded them, said the Lord.

For this is the covenant that I made with the house of Israel after these days, says the Lord: I will give my laws to their minds, and I will write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
And no longer shall each one teach his fellow citizen and each one his brother, saying, "Know God," but all shall know me, from the small to the great among them.
For I will be merciful to their falsehoods, and their lawless deeds and their sins I will remember no more.
When he says "new," he has made that first one old; and what is growing old and aging is near to destruction.
For that first law also had regulations for services, and that holy place of this world;
a tabernacle was set up, the first, in which were the lampstands and the table and the setting out of the bread, which was called "Holy."
Then, after that, the curtain of the tabernacle, and what was called "Holy of Holies."

It had a golden censer and the ark of the law, covered on the outside and the inside with gold, in which was a golden jar full of manna, and the rod of Aaron that sprouted, and the tablets of the law,
and above it the cherubim of glory, which overshadowed the mercy seat; of these things it is not now the time to speak in detail.
And these things having been set up in this way, the priests continually enter the outer tent and perform the service.
But into the inner one the high priest alone would enter, once a year, and not without blood, which he offers for himself and for the ignorance of the people.
By this the Holy Spirit made known that the way of the holy places had not yet been revealed, since the first tent still held its standing.
This was a parable of the time that was arriving, in which offerings and sacrifices were offered that could not make the one offering them perfect in heart,
but concerned only foods and drinks and various washings and ordinances of the flesh, until the time when the new dispensation should arrive.
But Christ came, the high priest of the good things to come, through the greater and more perfect tent, not made by hand, that is, not of this creation,
and not by the blood of goats and calves, but by his own blood he entered the sanctuary once and found eternal redemption.
If the blood of goats and bulls and the ashes of heifers, sprinkled on those who were defiled, purified them with respect to the purification of the flesh,
how much more will the blood of Christ, who through the Holy Spirit eternally offered himself spotless to God, purify your minds also from dead works to serve the living God!

And for this reason he is mediator of a new covenant, so that when a death has occurred for the redemption of the transgressions under the first law, those appointed to the eternal inheritance may receive the promise.
For where there is a written testament, death comes involuntarily upon the one who wrote the document,
because a written document is valid after death; otherwise it is never valid while the one who wrote the document is still alive.
For this reason not even the first covenant was inaugurated without blood.

For when all the commandments had been spoken by Moses to all the people according to the law, he took the blood of calves and goats with water, with scarlet wool and hyssop, and sprinkled the book itself and all the people,
and said: This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you.
And the tent itself and all the vessels of the service he likewise sprinkled with blood.
And all things were purified by blood according to the law, and without the shedding of blood there was no forgiveness.
Now if the figures of the heavenly things are purified by these, the heavenly things themselves are purified by better sacrifices than these.
For Christ did not enter holy places made by hand, figures of the true ones, but heaven itself, now to appear before the face of God on our behalf,
and not in order to offer himself many times, as the high priest enters the sanctuary once a year with the blood of another;
for then he would have had to suffer many times since the creation of the world. But now, once, at the end of the ages, he has appeared to bring sins to nothing by his sacrifice.
And just as it is appointed for human beings to die once, and after that comes judgment,
so also Christ was offered once to blot out the sins of many, and a second time he will appear, without sin, to those who await him in faith as Savior.

For the Law had a shadow of the good things to come, not the very image of the things. With the sacrifices that they offer year after year perpetually, it was never able to make those who offer them perfect.
If it were otherwise, they would surely have ceased from offering, because those who offer would no longer have had any suspicion of sins, having been cleansed once for all.
But in these sacrifices there is again a remembrance of sins year after year,
for the blood of goats and bulls cannot blot out sins.
Therefore, when he comes into the world, he says: "Offering and sacrifice you did not desire, but you have established a body for me.
A consecrated offering for sins you did not ask.
Then I said: Behold, I come; at the head of the books it is written of me, that I should do your will, O God."
Above he says: "Sacrifice, offering, and consecrated offering for sins you did not will, nor were you pleased with them," those that are offered according to the Law.
Then he said: "Behold, I come to do your will." He takes away the first in order to establish the second.
By this will we have been sanctified through the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once for all.
And every priest stands day after day at that service and offers the same sacrifice many times, sacrifices which can never take away sins.
But he himself offered a sacrifice once for all time and sat down at the right hand of God,
and from then on he waits until his enemies are placed under his feet.
For one sacrifice has been made perfect for all time for those who are sanctified.
And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after this saying,
namely: "This is my covenant that I will promise them after these days, says the Lord: I will give my laws to their minds, and on their hearts I will write them,
and their iniquities and their sins I will remember no more."
So where there is forgiveness of these, a sacrifice for sins is no longer needed.
So, brothers, we have confidence to enter the holy places by the blood of Jesus,
He who has renewed for us a new and living way through the veil, that is, through his flesh,
and a great high priest in the house of God:
let us draw near to him with a true heart and perfected faith, sprinkled in heart from evil suspicion
and washed in body with pure water. Let us hold fast rightly the confession of hope.
And let us consider one another, so as to stir one another up to love and good works.
Let us not abandon our own assembly, as is the custom of some, but give encouragement, and so much the more as you see that day drawing near.
For because of our willful sins after receiving the knowledge of the truth, a sacrifice for sins is no longer left [?],
but only a certain fearful expectation of judgment and a zeal of fire that will devour the enemies.
And whoever despises the law of Moses dies without mercy on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
How much worse a punishment is he worthy of who despises the Son of God, and counts as unworthy the blood of the covenant by which he was sanctified, and has insulted the Spirit of grace?
For we know him who said: Vengeance is mine, and I will repay, says the Lord. And again he says: The Lord will judge his people.
It is a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
Remember those former days, in which you were baptized and endured many struggles of suffering,
that is, in reproaches and afflictions you became a spectacle to the world, and that is, you shared with those who were living in these things;
for you also had mercy on the prisoners, and you counted the plundering of your produce as joy, knowing that you have for yourselves a better fruit, an eternal one, stored up in the heavens.
Do not cast away that openness of yours, which holds the gain of a great reward.
For you need patience, so that you may do the will of God and receive what was promised.
Yet a little while, a moment, and the one who is coming will come and will not delay.
But the righteous one will live by faith; and if you withdraw from him, my soul is not pleased.
But we are not of the withdrawal that leads to destruction, but of the faith that leads to the preservation of the soul.
Faith is the power of those who hope, the proof of things not seen.
For by this the elders were attested.
By faith we understand that the ages were established by the word of God, so that what is visible was made from what is not apparent.

[?] By faith Abel offered to God more abundant sacrifices than Cain, through which he was attested to be righteous, God bearing witness concerning his sacrifices; and because of this, though he died, he still speaks.
By faith Enoch was translated so that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God had translated him; and before his translation it was attested of him that he had pleased God.
But without faith it is impossible to please him; for whoever comes to God must believe that he exists, and that he is a rewarder of those who seek him.

By faith Noah, having received a command about things not yet seen, was afraid and made an ark for the salvation of his household, by which he condemned the world, and through that faith of righteousness he became an heir.
By faith Abraham, when he was called, obeyed and went out to the place that he was to receive as an inheritance; and he went out from there not knowing where he was going.
By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a foreign land, dwelling in a tent with Isaac and Jacob, his fellow heirs of the same promise;
for he was waiting for the city that has foundations laid, whose architect and maker is God.
By faith Sarah herself too, though she was barren, received power to conceive seed, and she gave birth when past the time of life, because she considered faithful the one who had promised her.
Therefore from one man, and him as good as dead, there were born descendants like the stars in multitude and like the innumerable sand of the sea.
By faith all these died, and they had not yet received what was promised, but they saw it from afar and greeted it, and confessed that they were strangers and passers-by on the earth.
For those who say such things make it plain that they are seeking a homeland.
And if they had been remembering the place from which they had come out, they would have had time to return there.
But now their heart speaks to them of a better one, that is, a heavenly one; therefore God was in no way ashamed of them, to be called their God, for he has prepared a city for them.
By faith he offered up Isaac at that testing, and he who had received the promise was offering up his only-begotten,
concerning whom it was said: "Through Isaac shall your descendants be named."
He reckoned thus, that God is able to raise up even from the dead, from where he also brought him back, in a figure.
By faith, concerning the things to come, Isaac blessed Jacob.
By faith Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of the sons of Joseph, and worshipped upon the top of his staff.
By faith Joseph, when he was reaching his end, made mention of the departure of the children of Israel and gave instructions concerning his bones.
By faith Moses, when he was born, was hidden for three months by his parents, for they saw that the child was fair, and they did not fear the command of the king.
By faith Moses, when he had grown up, refused to be called a son of Pharaoh's daughter,
choosing rather to suffer evil together with the people of God than to have the fleeting pleasure of sin;
he reckoned the reproach of Christ as greater riches than the treasures of Egypt, for he was looking to the repayment of the reward.
By faith he left Egypt and did not fear the wrath of the king, for he reckoned the invisible one as if he were seen.
By faith he performed the Passover and the sprinkling of the blood, so that the destroyer of the firstborn would not touch them.
By faith they crossed the Red Sea as if on dry land, which the Egyptians attempted and were drowned.
By faith the walls of Jericho fell by being encircled for seven days.
By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish together with the disobedient, for she received the spies in peace.
And what more shall I say? For time fails me to tell of Gideon, of Barak, of Samson and of Jephthah, of David and of Samuel and of the prophets,

who by faith overcame kings: Abraham and the judges; who worked righteousness: Abraham, Moses, Joshua and Phinehas; who obtained the promise: Abraham, Joshua and Caleb; who stopped the mouths of lions: Samson, David and Daniel;

who quenched the power of fire: the three youths, Hananiah, Azariah and Mishael; who escaped the edge of the sword: Uriah the priest and Elijah the prophet; who were made strong out of weakness: Hezekiah, Samson and Joshua; who became mighty in battle: Abraham, Lot, Moses and Joshua; who routed the camps of foreigners: Gideon, Barak, Samson and David;

women received their dead raised up: the Shunammite and the woman of Zarephath. But others died under various tortures and did not accept deliverance, so that they might be made worthy of a better resurrection: the seven Maccabean brothers and their mother, and other prophets;
some were tried by torments and scourging: Elisha, Jeremiah and Job; and then again by chains and prisons: Jeremiah and Micah;

Jeremiah and Naboth were crushed with stones; Isaiah was sawn apart; Job and Zerubbabel were put to the test; Micah, Amos and Zechariah the priest were slain by death of the sword; John the Baptist, Elijah and Elisha went about in mantles and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, ill-treated,
of whom this world was not worthy, wandering astray in the wilderness, on mountains, in caves and in holes of the earth, the prophets whom Obadiah fed in the wilderness.
And all of these were attested through faith, and yet they did not receive what had been promised,
for God had determined beforehand something better for us, so that they should not be made perfect apart from us.

Now therefore, since we too have so great a multitude of witnesses surrounding us, let us cast away every weight and the sin that comes on us so swiftly, and let us run with endurance the contest set before us.
And let us look to the leader and perfecter of our faith, Jesus, who for the joy set before him endured the cross, despised the shame, and sat down at the right hand of the thrones of God.
Consider him who endured such contradiction from sinners against himself, so that you may not grow weary in your souls and lose heart.
You have not yet stood bravely against sin to the point of blood,
and you have lost heart from the consolation which speaks to you as to sons: My son, do not be faint-hearted at the discipline of the Lord, nor give way when you are reproved by him.
for the Lord disciplines those he loves, and he punishes every son whom he accepts."
Endure discipline, for God receives you as sons. What son is there whom the father does not discipline?
If you are far from discipline, in which all have shared, then you are strangers and not sons.
And now, if we have had fleshly fathers as instructors and we revered them, shall we not all the more submit to the Father of spirits and live?
For they disciplined for a few days according to their own will, but he does so for what is better, so that they may receive of his holiness.
No discipline brings joy at the time it is given, only sorrow. Later, though, it produces the peaceful fruit of righteousness in those who have been trained by it.
Therefore lift up the drooping hands and the weakened knees,
And make straight the paths of your feet, so that the lame may not fall but rather be healed.
Pursue peace with all, and holiness, for without this no one will see the Lord.
Take care that no one falls short of the grace of God, that no troubling root of bitterness springs up in anyone, and that through it many are not defiled.
Let no one be a fornicator or vile, like Esau, who for one meal sold his birthright.
You know that afterward he wished to inherit the blessing and was rejected, for he found no place for repentance, even though he sought it with tears.
For you have not come to the mountain that can be touched with the hand and that burned with fire, and to gloom and darkness and mist,
where there was the blast of the trumpet and the sound of words, which those who heard refused, asking that no further word be added for them.
For they could not bear what was commanded: if even a beast touched the mountain, it was to be driven off with stones.
And so terrible was that sight that Moses said, "I am afraid and trembling."
But you have come to Mount Zion and the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to the assembly of myriads of angels,
and to the church of the firstborn, enrolled in the heavens, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of the righteous who have been made perfect,
and to Jesus, the mediator of the new covenant, and to the sprinkling of blood, which is better than what was spoken by Abel.
Take heed, lest you turn away from the one who speaks. For if those did not escape who turned away on earth from the command, how much less shall we, if we turn away from the heavenly one,
whose voice then shook the earth, and now he has said and says: Yet once more I will shake not only the earth, but also the heavens.
But this "once" shows the change of the things that are shaken, as of created things, so that what is unshakable may remain.
Therefore let us hold fast to the unshakable kingdom; we have grace, by which we serve God pleasingly, with fear and reverence,
for indeed our God is a consuming fire.
Let brotherly love remain among you.
Do not forget love of strangers, for through this some, as it were without knowing it, have entertained angels as guests.
Remember those who are in bonds, as though you were bound together with them, and those who are ill-treated, for you too have bodies.
Marriage is honorable in every way and the bed undefiled; but fornicators and adulterers God will judge.
Be free of the love of silver in your way of life; be content with what you have; for: Neither will I abandon you.
Now therefore it is fitting to say this: The Lord is my helper, I will not be afraid; what will man do to me?
Remember your leaders, who spoke to you the words of God; observe the outcome of their life and imitate their faith.
Jesus Christ yesterday and today, and he himself is forever.
Do not accept teaching that is manifold and strange, for it is good that you are strengthened in the heart by grace and not by foods, by which those who walked in them gained nothing.
We have an altar from which those who served the tabernacle have no right to eat.
For the animals whose blood is offered for sins in the sanctuary by the high priest, their bodies were burned outside the camp.
For this reason Jesus also, that he might sanctify the people with his own blood, suffered outside the gates.
Now therefore let us go out to him outside the camp and bear his reproach.
For we do not have here a city to dwell in, but we seek the one to come.
Therefore we offer the sacrifice of praise continually to God, that is, the fruit of lips and the confession of his name.
But do not forget the doing of good and sharing, for such sacrifices are pleasing to God.

Obey your leaders and submit to them, for they keep watch over your souls, as those who will give an account; so that they may do this with joy and not with sighing, for this would not be easy for you.
Pray for us also; we trust that we have a good mind toward all and wish to conduct ourselves well.
I beseech you all the more to do this, so that I may come to you soon.
And the God of peace, who brought up from the dead the great shepherd of the sheep by the blood of the eternal covenant, our Lord Jesus,
May he establish you in every good thing, to do his will, he who works what is pleasing to him among us, before him, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory for ever and ever. Amen.
I beseech you, brothers, bear with this word of entreaty, although I have written to you briefly.
You know that Timothy, our brother, whom I have sent away; with him, if he comes soon, I will see you.
Greet all your leaders and all the saints. Those who are from Italy greet you.
The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
